newsitem.title: USA: Maxim sees drop in order cancellations.
newsitem.headline: Maxim sees drop in order cancellations.

text.p: Maxim Integrated Products Inc Wednesday said it expected a reduction in customer cancellations its second fiscal quarter to the end of December.
The company had $23 million in customer cancellations during the first quarter ended September 30 and $32.6 million in the previous three months.

"Since Q1 cancellation rates have reduced from Q496 levels, we also believe that customer inventory adjustments are approaching an end," the company said in a statement accompanying its first-quarter financial results.
"Based on current Q2 order cancellation rates, we expect to have less total cancellations in Q2 than in any of the previous three quarters," it said.

The Sunnyvale, Calif.-based maker of analog products reported a first-quarter profit of $31.4 million, or $0.45 a share, compared with $22.6 million, or $0.32, for the first quarter of fiscal 1996. Revenue rose to $101 million from $96.4 million for the same period a year ago.

The company said backlog shippable in the next 12 months continued to decline, ending at $103 million. Orders requested for near-term delivery represent a higher percentage of current backlog than a year ago.

"Of our ending Q197 backlog, 72 percent is shippable in the next three months, compared to 59 percent in Q496. The company also experienced a substantial increase in turns orders over Q496 levels," referring to customer orders that are for delivery within the same quarter and can be shipped within the quarter if the company has matching inventory.
"In Q297, weekly booking rates have increased to the point that they are now approaching our Q197 revenue levels," the company said.

"While higher booking and lower cancellation rates are encouraging, our ability to maintain and increase revenues from Q197 levels is dependent upon the turns orders the company receives during Q2 and the degree to which those orders match with inventories that are available for shipment within the current quarter," it said.
"Further revenue growth in Q3 and Q4 will be dependent upon booking rates continuing to increase from current levels."
